About 20,000 residents of Nuevo Laredo may need to update their INE voter credential by January 25, 2027, because of an electoral-section reorganization — even if they have not moved — according to El Mañana de Nuevo Laredo.

The reorganization means some voters' electoral sections have changed, and a credential that no longer matches the voter's current section could leave them unable to vote in 2027, the paper reports. Residents are advised to check whether their section changed and, if so, update the credential at the INE module.

To update, voters need to bring a birth certificate, a photo ID, and a recent proof of address to the INE module, according to the report. The paper frames the update as a simple step that protects the right to vote — one worth taking well before the January deadline, rather than waiting until the final days.

What to watch next: whether the INE module extends hours or adds capacity as the deadline approaches, and how many of the roughly 20,000 affected residents complete the update in time.

Sources: El Mañana de Nuevo Laredo, “¿Cómo actualizar tu credencial del INE para no quedarte sin votar en el 2027?; requisitos y fechas,” October 25, 2026.
